_weather_hex_chart.source: Vaults of Vaarn, Referee's Toolbox pp.155-156 (Weather) - chart transcribed from the p.156 figure 2026-06-12

effects.Still: The desert is still. Visibility is good. No modifiers.
effects.Hazy: Lurid mists hang over the desert; landmarks cannot be seen from a distance. Vigilance checks at DIS.
effects.Dust Storm: Visibility badly impaired; travel possible at HALF speed (a 3-day journey takes 6). Vigilance checks at DIS.
effects.Sand Storm: Nobody travels: hunker down and wait it out (tents/makeshift shelter are adequate protection). Any encounters rolled today are sheltering from the storm in the same place as the party. Beam weapons are not effective during sandstorms.
effects.Heatwave: PCs must consume twice their normal ration of water per day if they wish to travel.
effects.Worm-pollen: Half travel speed through the sticky spore-drifts; worm-pollen is edible - treat worm-pollen days as providing d4 rations per player.
effects.Rain: A rare bounty: the party may collect 2d6 days of rations per member. A short-lived imperium of majestic flora follows.
effects.Prismatic Tempest: No travel of any kind; PCs take 3d6 electrical damage every hour spent aboveground.

fields.Faith: Vaa, Blue Goddess of Empty Spaces

fields.Detail: Ancient device generating mass from air, thousands of times faster than mortal craftsmen. Most fabricate a single object; settlement is overrun with that object.
Known for breeding packbeasts (burden birds, zorses, weeping lizards). Healthy trained animals for sale; weekly races with betting.
Residence of a Vaarnish Oracle whose wisdom is unquestioned and eccentricities tolerated. Generate Oracle from sub-table.
Large monastery/temple exercising political and economic influence. Monks follow settlement's dominant faith.
Built around a holy site: Autarch's grave, Solar Saint's bones, fabled fountain. Pilgrims arrive from across Vaarn.
Famous for quality of drinks, skill of musicians, or rudeness of barkeep.
Proudly maintained orchards. Water consumption astronomical; trees considered worth any price.
Gladiatorial arena. Famed gladiators live luxuriously; losers die in sick beds or pauper's graves.
Paradoxical architecture: innocuous houses cavernous inside, uphill aqueducts, inverted ziggurats. May be active or shunned as cursed.
Built around a spacecraft forming infrastructure or decorative feature. Can no longer fly; citizens wish it could.
Ingress to the chrome caverns lies within settlement — cellar stairs descending too far, or a vast blast-door structure opening only at rulers' command.
Refuse dump of imperious depth with its own ecosystem. Stench notable from a day's travel. Undercaste maintains it, beats back fungal insurgencies.
One of few functional synth repair facilities left. Operational ReadMe consoles, supercooled parts storage. Overrun with damaged synths; rulers charge for access.
College for esoteric study. Blindfolded acolytes; psionic demonstrations light up the sky. Mystics claim detachment from mundane matters but influence government.
Great healing house at auspicious astral confluence or above restorative hot spring. Ancient surgeon-witch order. Rare-disease cures available for a price.
Large defended workshop brewing Wondrous Elixirs. Master Alchemist is capricious; those bearing rare components are better received.
Great theatre; citizens are thespians or audience. Plays staged every night: Fallen Autarchy tragedies, Neo-Neo-Relativist monologues, Lunan choral satires. Government intertwined with theatre.
Expansive verdant pleasure garden with ornamental foliage. Cultural life revolves around it. Vast water investment to prevent withering.
Resident religious hermit on a colossal pillar. Given rations via pulleys. Periodically emerges (naked, mad) to harangue crowd and preach end times.
One of the surviving orbital cannons — a vast crowned Autarch head in tarnished gold. Eyes track stars; occasionally belches micro-missile clouds into the sky. Air traffic avoids the settlement.
Political upheaval. Roll again on government types for insurgent system. For each NPC generated, roll even = loyal to old, odd = supports nascent system.
Deep bigotry from majority population type towards minority. If homogeneous, bigotry revolves around petty obscure difference.
Disease runs rampant. Infected are shunned; dead buried in mass graves without normal rituals.
Nanomachine infection runs rampant, resists all cures. Infected shunned from fear.
Those who die within the settlement do not stay dead. Cause unclear; all burials outside walls.
Harried by a nearby monster lair. Generate at max population for lair type.
Harried by nearby bandits (see Bandit Camp). Cutting off trade, may raid inside walls.
Internal feud between two family groups (or voluntary clubs for ancestries without families). All social/political life concentrated on furthering it.
Food source under threat or failed; stores running low. May be concealed by rulers.
Water source under threat or dried up; reserves running low. May be concealed by rulers.
Population ageing; reproduction has failed for the resident ancestries. Newcomers also unable to produce offspring. Cause unknown.
Subject to an angry Quantum Daemon's improbable, poetic curse.
Infested with Vaarnish Unicorns. They breed fast, eat everything, leave glittering dung. Cannot be exterminated faster than they reappear.
Inhabitants troubled by worsening shared dream. PCs who sleep in settlement also begin to experience it.
Settlement pays tribute to a Cacklemaw Clan. War Mama visits yearly; her demands have ballooned beyond what can be given.
Obsessive violent search for hidden internal enemies. Accused get mock trials, ostracism, or execution.
Outside group has infiltrated. Sabotage, impersonation, paranoia. Seat of government may already be infiltrated.
Dominant religion challenged by upstart faith. Roll again on dominant religion table. Each NPC: even = believer in dominant faith, odd = supports new.
Subject to a local Faa Nomad Tribe vendetta. Faa refuse aid to anyone connected with the settlement; may strangle trade or sabotage water sources.
Preparing for open warfare with a neighbour (existing on map or distant rival).
Two formerly friendly NPCs argued about something trivial; no longer speaking.
Bandits raided, seized goods, fled into wilderness.
Pivotal government NPC has died. Murder or natural; nothing will be the same.
Razed by catastrophe. Survivors hide in basements/attics.
A building burned down. Arson or accident is unclear.
A much-liked resident turned up dead. Culprit unknown; theories proliferate.
A delirious stranger was found in the desert near the walls. Recovering under guard. Rumours abound.
Some new fad or pastime is in vogue.
Pre-existing government overthrown; new system in place.
Dominant religion overthrown; new belief system dominant.
A new NPC has moved in.
New romance (covert or open) between two resident NPCs.
New tavern or cafe; everyone gathers there.
NPC receives religious visions; preaches night and day. People are listening.
Daemon has manifested. Local NPC fallen under its influence — gone 'mad' pursuing bizarre quantum tasks.
Rival party has arrived. Everyone seems to like them a little more than you.
A house broken into; sentimental items stolen. Resident suspected but unknown.
Minor NPC taken sick; no longer performs previous duties.
Trade caravan from distant market city of Gnomon has arrived bearing rare goods.
Settlement's existing problem has radically worsened.
